title: The Uncomfortable Truth
hook: One hard admission, then 3 quiet minutes before anyone repairs it.
steps: Say your pause phrase. Choose who speaks first. The second turn gets the same clock.
A quiet minute, then one difficult admission. If the listener speaks, the only line is, "I'm taking this in."
When you stop, start 3 minutes. No fix, bright side, cross-examination, or matching confession. If the quiet feels like a wall, repeat that sentence only.
Ask for one short reply and name the kind: what you heard, one question, or an idea. Or end the turn. Then swap.
ending: One truth each, under this rule, finishes the standard sitting.
pass: A pass or a smaller admission is a finished turn. The pause phrase can stop you or send you to an easier truth.
safety: Do not build a case against your partner. Ongoing harm, abuse, or a safety problem stops this frame. Ordinary responsibility resumes.

title: The Permission Slip
hook: Sign permission to be unfinished in one specific way. Your partner may hear the sentence. They do not grant it.
steps: Glance at the menu or ignore it: imperfect, playful, uncertain, ambitious, needy, emotionally open. Draft in silence.
Standard shape: I give myself permission to be [one way] when [a real situation], and I will stop requiring [one self-demand] of myself this week.
Read it to yourself. If their body, time, or money is the object, keep the permission and set the request aside. A later request can be declined.
Read aloud only if you want to. The witness says what they heard, then stops. They do not rewrite it or grant it. Then swap. A card may stay unread.
ending: Done when each person who wanted a slip has signed one or chosen not to show it.
pass: You may pass, pocket the card, or change the word. One honest permission is enough.

title: Confession Without Consequence
hook: Offer one harmless embarrassment, regret, insecurity, or private oddity. Curious questions only.
steps: Name the four kinds. Agree a pause word. "Different item" is enough.
Before the story, say, "This is mine to tell, and it is harmless," and name the kind. If you cannot, it leaves the game. Tell it in 3 to 5 minutes.
Two curious questions, not a case and not advice. A declined question is replaced, or you stop at one.
Close the turn. Swap with equal time. The second person may pass, and does not owe a more dramatic kind.
ending: Done when each allowed offer, or a pass, has been heard inside the rule.
pass: Either of you may pass or decline a question. The pause word changes the item.
safety: If harm shows up, say, "This leaves the game." Abuse, a betrayal they have a right to know, an undisclosed health or legal risk, harm to someone else, infidelity, and illegal acts stay outside.

title: When I Feel Small
hook: Name when you feel inadequate or overlooked, and the response that has actually helped.
steps: About 8 private minutes. Two recognizable situations. For each, one helping behavior and one that bounces. "Love me more" is too vague. Unsure is allowed. A guess is labeled a guess.
Share one situation and both responses, as written. Your partner repeats the help in their words, then says can, sometimes, or not really. No demonstration unless you ask.
Correct them if they polished your sentence into a nicer one. Then swap. Stop after one situation each.
ending: Done when the help has been repeated and answered with a real limit.
pass: You may pass, shrink a situation, or leave what bounces unspoken. A pass finishes the turn.
safety: If the situation is a harmful pattern, they restate and do not cross-examine. Stopping it is a separate conversation.

title: No Armor Tonight
hook: For a short window, set down joke-as-cover, defense, and the impressive answer. One modest topic, spoken plainly.
steps: Say the topic in one sentence. Set about 15 minutes, and split it in half.
Talk about the feeling. If a joke ducks it, say, "Let me try that plainly," and restate one sentence. Your partner does not catch it for you. A delighted laugh may stay.
At the half, the listener offers one feeling of their own about what they heard. Not a score of how bare you were.
Swap for the same length. End when the timer ends, or sooner. There is no armor score.
ending: A plain sentence is enough. After the timer, the evening may be funny again.
pass: Either of you may end early or trade for a milder topic.
safety: An insult is not unarmored truth. If the topic becomes harm or safety, stop the style game and deal with it directly.
